name: Segmented Nav
summary: A pill navigation where one indicator travels between items rather than each item lighting up, with full arrow-key navigation and re-measurement on resize, font load and scroll.

attempts.prompt: Build a segmented navigation control with a sliding indicator.
attempts.problem: Gave each item its own background and crossfaded between them, which is not a sliding indicator at all — nothing travels, two things fade. When rewritten with a single moving element, the indicator was positioned once on load, so it sat in the wrong place as soon as the container was resized, and landed a few pixels off on first paint because it measured before the webfont had loaded and changed every item's width.

attempts.prompt: Fix the measurement and make it keyboard accessible.
attempts.problem: Added a resize listener but still measured against the viewport rather than the element, so it missed changes when the container resized without the window changing. Keyboard support was Tab only: arrow keys, which are what people actually reach for in a segmented control, did nothing, and the indicator animated from zero width on first paint because the initial placement was not exempted from the transition.

finalPrompt:
Build a segmented navigation control in plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript, no dependencies.

Use one indicator element that travels between items. Do not give each item its own background and crossfade them — the movement is the component. Position it with translate and width driven by custom properties, so the transition is on transform and size rather than on layout offsets.

Measurement is the real work. The indicator must be correct after all of these: first paint, the webfont loading and changing every item's width, the container resizing, and the strip being scrolled horizontally when it overflows. Use a ResizeObserver on the nav element itself rather than a window resize listener, await document.fonts.ready, and re-place on the nav's own scroll event.

The first placement must not animate. Disable the transition, set the position, then restore the transition on the next animation frame — otherwise the indicator slides in from zero width on load. Keep the indicator at zero opacity until it has been placed once.

Keyboard: arrow left and right move between items and wrap at both ends, Home and End jump to first and last, and each moves focus and selection together. Call preventDefault on all four.

Mark the active item with aria-current="page" rather than a class, and style from that attribute.

Use a spring-like easing, cubic-bezier(.34, 1.4, .3, 1), so the indicator overshoots slightly and settles. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove the travel transition but keep the fade.

Emit a bubbling CustomEvent named sn:change carrying the selected label so a host page can react without editing the component.

Colour comes only from CSS custom properties: var(--surface), var(--border), var(--text), var(--text-dim), var(--accent), var(--accent-fg). No literal hex, rgb or hsl values.
why:
The first prompt failed on a definition. "Sliding indicator" describes an appearance, and the cheapest thing that matches the description is a crossfade — which produces something that looks vaguely right in a screenshot and wrong in motion. Saying what must not be built, and why the movement is the point, was the only thing that fixed it.

The rest is measurement, and measurement bugs share a pattern: they are all about *when*, not *how*. The formula never changes; what changes is how many moments you remember to recompute at. Listing those moments explicitly — first paint, font load, container resize, strip scroll — produced correct code immediately, where asking to "fix the measurement" produced a window resize listener that misses most of them.

The no-animation-on-first-placement rule is the kind of detail that separates a component that feels built from one that feels generated, and it is never volunteered.
